content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge grounded an UNDERDETERMINED verdict on a single verse's admitting both readings, which is exactly the ground the rule forbids.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that admits both readings, with nothing else settling it, is such a verse.", "room": "\"with nothing else settling it\" -- reading (a): the judge's added clauses about [CR3] LINK 4, [CR2] §5 and [DR3] C2 show it weighed the parties' whole support, not just the one verse; reading (b): the judge's operative and leading ground is that Matthew 1:16 itself admits both readings and the mutual answers left it unsettled, which is precisely the condition the rule says can never support UNDERDETERMINED. Reading (b) controls, because the stated reason is the verse's two-readings ambiguity and the added clauses serve only to confirm that nothing else settled it.", "why": "The judge made a verse that admits both readings, with nothing else settling it, the stated ground for UNDERDETERMINED, the exact move K-S2 forbids."}
